subject: Simple example of a user defined class that does not work.

messages.author: f82eb6cf01e30a21
messages.subject: Simple example of a user defined class that does not work.
parts:
Dear TMB users,


I am interested in developing an agent based model in TMB. 
It would be helpful to be able to define my own classes.  
I have tried to make a class that can do linear regression; sadly it does not work. 
I know that I am probably doing something quite foolish; still a simple example of how to make a class may help even those more clever than I.  
It may even expand the number of people making useful TMB libraries.
Thank you for your help.

Aaron

The c++ code "regression.cpp"


#include <TMB.hpp>
template<class Type>

class nll
{ // initalize a class called nll
public:
  nll(  vector<Type> tx,  vector<Type>ty,  Type ta,Type tb, Type tlog_sigma);
  vector<Type> tx;     // just some stuff stored in the class
  vector<Type> ty;
  Type ta;
  Type tb;
  Type tlog_sigma;
  ~nll(); //class killer!
  Type computenll();//lets try to compute the likelihood
};

 
void  nll::nll(x, y, a, b, tlog_sigma;)
 { //initialize nll class something is clearly wrong
   //I am pretty sure that I am not initializing tx,ty,ta,tb,tlog_sigma correctly
 tx=x; 
 ty=y;
 ta=a;
 tb=b;
 tlog_sigma=log_sigma;
 };

void nll:: ~nll()
{ // All classes must DIE!
   std::cout<<"yo!"<<std::endl;
 }


Type nll::computenll()
  { //compute nll
    Type sigma = exp(tlog_sigma); //convert from log space
     int n = ty.size(); // get number of data points to loop over
     Type cnll = 0.0; // initialize negative log likelihood don't want to call it the same as the class      
     for(int i = 0; i < n; i++){ 
       cnll -= dnorm(ty[i], ta + tb * tx[i], sigma, true);
     } 
     return cnll;//we want to return the nll
  };


// linear regression


Type objective_function<Type>::operator() () {
  //input data
DATA_VECTOR(x);
DATA_VECTOR(y);

// define parameters:
PARAMETER(a); // intercept
PARAMETER(b); // slope
PARAMETER(log_sigma); // log(residual SD)


 Type N=0.0;//initalize main nll 
 nll::nll(x,y,a,b,log_sigma); //initialize nll class
 N=nll::computenll(); // compute nll
 return N; 

 
};


The associated R code 

library(TMB)
compile("regression.cpp")
dyn.load(dynlib("regression"))

set.seed(123) //make data
x <- runif(20, 1, 10)
y <- rnorm(20, mean = 1.8 + 2.4 * x, sd = exp(0.3))
plot(x, y)

//do the stuff
obj <- MakeADFun(
  data = list(x = x, y = y), 
  parameters = list(a = 0, b = 0, log_sigma = 0),
  DLL = "regression")
opt <- nlminb(start = obj$par, obj = obj$fn, gr = obj$gr)
rep <- sdreport(obj)

Aaron,

Looks like you've at least got a couple typos in nll:nll(...) in the code you provided. Should be "void  nll::nll(x, y, a, b, log_sigma)", not "void  nll::nll(x, y, a, b, tlog_sigma;)". 

Buck
